questions.text: How do you run a threat model for a new feature? Walk me through a recent example.

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which threats did you identify, and which did you rank as most serious?
How did the threat model change the design or the release?

scoring_rubric.2: Lists generic threats without the feature context
scoring_rubric.3: Maps data flows and trust boundaries for the feature
scoring_rubric.4: Ranks risks and agrees mitigations with the team
scoring_rubric.5: Also tracks mitigations to completion and updates the model as the design evolves

questions.text: How would you review cloud IAM permissions for a team that has grown by accident over several years?

follow_up_suggestions.text: How would you find which permissions are actually used?
How do you remove access without breaking production?

scoring_rubric.3: Uses usage data and least-privilege principles
scoring_rubric.4: Plans a phased reduction with owners and rollback
scoring_rubric.5: Also automates reviews and sets guardrails for new access

questions.text: Describe how you would handle a suspected data leak discovered on a Friday evening.

follow_up_suggestions.text: What would you do in the first hour, and what would you avoid doing?
Who needs to be told, and in what order?

scoring_rubric.2: Reacts without containment or evidence preservation
scoring_rubric.3: Contains the issue, preserves evidence and escalates
scoring_rubric.4: Coordinates legal, communications and engineering with clear roles
scoring_rubric.5: Also runs a blameless review and turns findings into lasting controls

questions.text: How do you help a development team fix a security finding without slowing their delivery?

follow_up_suggestions.text: How do you decide which findings must be fixed before release?
What do you do when a team disagrees about the risk?

scoring_rubric.1: Sees security as a blocker only
scoring_rubric.2: Reports findings without help to fix them
scoring_rubric.3: Prioritises by risk and explains fixes clearly
scoring_rubric.4: Offers secure defaults and reusable fixes to reduce future work
scoring_rubric.5: Also builds shared tooling and training, and records risk decisions openly

questions.text: What controls do you put in place to protect secrets used by applications and build pipelines?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Where are the secrets stored, and who can read them?
How do you rotate secrets without downtime?

scoring_rubric.2: Mentions a vault without access controls
scoring_rubric.3: Uses a managed store, least-privilege access and scanning for leaks
scoring_rubric.4: Adds rotation, short-lived credentials and audit logging
scoring_rubric.5: Also covers supply-chain controls and recovery when a secret is exposed
